comparison: Perfect match (Jaccard=1.0) on claims C23-C30 regarding positioning relative to prior work. Both evaluations find the integration of multiple theoretical frameworks well-supported with appropriate citations. OpenEval emphasizes the clear articulation of distinctions from prior work, while peer reviewers acknowledge this is not merely a compendium but involves necessary adaptations.

Perfect match (Jaccard=1.0) on claims C32, C35, C37, C39 connecting theoretical predictions to experimental observations. Both evaluations support the alignment between theory and cited experimental data (Köndgen et al. 2008, Ulrich 2002). Neither raises concerns about the empirical grounding of these claims.

Perfect match (Jaccard=1.0) on claims C44-C51 connecting NLA framework to motor control. Both evaluations support the integration with motor control literature and cited experimental evidence (Dimitriou & Edin 2010, Papaioannou & Dimitriou 2021). Peer reviewers note this helps understand cortical organization.

Perfect match (Jaccard=1.0) on claims C72, C77, C80, C83, C86 regarding microcircuit implementation. Both evaluations support Theorem 2, MNIST learning results, and parameter-free learning claims. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the credit assignment solution via apical-compartment interneurons and mathematical proofs.

Strong match (Jaccard=0.833) on claims C87-C91 regarding contribution significance. Both evaluations support the mathematical demonstration of local-global error connection and the framework's predictive nature. Peer reviewers position this as 'likely an important step towards a comprehensive theory' while noting readability challenges and remaining assumptions.

Strong match (Jaccard=0.75) on claims C69-C71 regarding advantages over non-lookahead networks. Both evaluations support the necessity of prospective coding for real-time learning with brief stimuli. Peer reviewers emphasize this captures observations not explained by prior theories.

Good match (Jaccard=0.667) on claims C62-C63 regarding learning complex temporal correlations in iEEG data. Both evaluations support the simulation results demonstrating the model's capabilities. Peer reviewers note 'multiple and diverse simulations' and 'solid evidence' without specific challenges.

Good match (Jaccard=0.667) on claims C93-C94 regarding sequential learning and sleep-phase dynamics. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature, while peer reviewers also express UNCERTAIN, noting 'thorny assumptions' about unobserved details of learning rules and soma-dendrite interactions without explicit validation.

Good match (Jaccard=0.667) on claims C103-C104 regarding future applications. Both evaluations support these as reasonable speculative extensions. OpenEval notes they are well-motivated but represent future work; peer reviewers accept them as appropriate discussion content without challenge.

Moderate match (Jaccard=0.6) on claims C9-C17 regarding theoretical motivation and relationship to physics principles. Both evaluations support the historical contextualization and conceptual foundations. Peer reviewers explicitly discuss the Lagrangian/Hamiltonian analogy. OpenEval notes the biological justification for prospective coding (C16) remains speculative.

Moderate match (Jaccard=0.5) on claims C100-C102 connecting NLA to broader neuroscience observations. Both evaluations support these connections with cited experimental evidence across multiple neural systems. Peer reviewers emphasize the theory 'captures a more extensive range of observations' than previous frameworks.

Moderate match (Jaccard=0.438) on core theoretical framework claims C1-C8. Both evaluations strongly support the mathematical formulation and internal consistency. Peer reviewers affirm this as a core contribution linking predictive coding, error-based learning, and neuronal dynamics. OpenEval covers C1-C8 while peer review focuses on C2-C8 plus additional claims C13, C16-C22.

Moderate match (Jaccard=0.429) on claims C95-C98 regarding integration of prior theoretical frameworks. Both evaluations support the characterization of relationships to prior work. Peer reviewers note the theory 'captures a more extensive range of observations' and acknowledge necessary adaptations beyond simple aggregation.

Partial overlap (Jaccard=0.333) on claims C18-C22 regarding core computational mechanism. OpenEval evaluates C18-C22 as SUPPORTED with emphasis on mathematical rigor and Theorem 1. Peer review R1 includes these claims within a broader set (C2-C22) and affirms the theoretical framework as a core contribution with solid evidence.
